chunks.subject: AP Physics 2
chunks.title: Q4 Qualitative Quantitative Translation (QQT) — 8 points
chunks.content: AP Physics 2 FRQ 4 is Qualitative Quantitative Translation (QQT), 8 points, scored by lettered sub-points. The QQT task requires connecting qualitative reasoning with quantitative analysis around a claim. Q4 topic: waves (e.g., wave behavior, interference, or optics). Points reward: a correct claim/prediction, qualitative reasoning citing the relevant wave principle, a consistent quantitative expression/derivation, and agreement between the qualitative and quantitative arguments. Common failure: a claim without a supporting principle; quantitative work inconsistent with the qualitative reasoning; misapplying the wave relationship.

chunks.subject: AP Physics 2
chunks.title: Q4 exemplar — Sample 4A, 7/8
chunks.content: Q4 (QQT) scored 7/8 — a correct claim, sound qualitative wave reasoning, and a mostly consistent quantitative argument, losing one sub-point on a minor inconsistency or incomplete step. Illustrates a near-complete qualitative–quantitative link.

chunks.subject: AP Physics 2
chunks.title: Q4 exemplar — Sample 4B, 6/8
chunks.content: Q4 (QQT) scored 6/8 — earned the claim and qualitative reasoning plus most of the quantitative argument, losing a couple of sub-points where the quantitative support was incomplete. Illustrates a solid response short of full consistency.

chunks.subject: AP Physics 2
chunks.title: Q4 exemplar — Sample 4C, 2/8
chunks.content: Q4 (QQT) scored 2/8 — earned only a couple of sub-points (e.g., a claim or one reasoning step), losing the principle-based reasoning and the quantitative support. Illustrates a response that cannot connect qualitative and quantitative wave reasoning.
